claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex!

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex? This generally means he lives with you, or you contribute to the cost of looking after him at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help support him financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes, food, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation a bit more.

Could you tell me who Alex currently lives with? For example, does he live with another parent, a relative, or someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying.

Is Alex's mum (your ex-partner) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Are you (or your ex-partner) ordinarily resident in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you! And just to confirm regarding your ex-partner as well - is she also living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she lives in the UK too.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the eligibility rules.

One more important question: You mentioned you contribute towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, food, school supplies, etc.). Would you say your contributions are at least equal to the current Child Benefit amount? 

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child. So your contributions would need to be at least around that amount (whether paid weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum covering a set period).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute more than that. I give about £26 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's very helpful.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of my assessment:

**For Alex:**
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old (he's 8)
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ You contribute £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate (£25.60 per week for an only or eldest child)
- ✅ No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you still qualify because you're contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep. This meets the requirement of being "responsible" for a child.

**A couple of things to be aware of:**
1. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If Alex's mum decides to claim in the future, you would need to agree between yourselves who should receive it.
2. If your individual income is over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement for Child Benefit. Although Alex does not live with his father (the claimant), the claimant contributes £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, food, school supplies). This exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week. According to the rules, you can qualify for Child Benefit if you are 'paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them'. Additionally, since Alex's mother is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him, there is no competing claim. Both the claimant and Alex's mother live in the UK. Therefore, the claimant meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.
